Arctic exploration. European explorers from the sixteenth century onward sought the elusive Northwest Passage through northern Canada, a shortcut to Asian trade that became the obsession of centuries. Henry Hudson made multiple Arctic voyages seeking this passage but died in mutiny and ice. Roald Amundsen successfully navigated it from nineteen oh-three to nineteen oh-six, proving its existence. The quest revealed the region's hostile climate, indigenous peoples' deep knowledge, and later strategic importance during the Cold War.
